sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2-Codex
sources.evidence: Dated December 18, 2025; releases this GPT-5.2 coding variant across Codex surfaces for paid ChatGPT users that day, with API access forthcoming. Describes vision, tool use and context compaction. Reopened October 27 for parameters: explicitly calls GPT-5.2-Codex a version of GPT-5.2 further optimized for coding; improved vision and compaction are described, but no numerical total or active size, pruning, distillation or expert expansion is stated.

sources.title: GPT-5.2-Codex model reference
sources.evidence: Exact model reference: GPT-5.2 variant; text and image input, text output; 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens; low/medium/high/xhigh reasoning; Responses, function calling and prompt caching. The undated default identifier is gpt-5.2-codex; current status is Shut down. Fresh exact-model documentation read on October 27 confirms the named GPT-5.2 lineage but supplies neither a total nor an active parameter count.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: January 14, 2026 entry explicitly releases gpt-5.2-codex to Responses. February 3 says the faster inference stack did not change the model or its weights.

sources.title: Addendum to GPT-5.2 System Card: GPT-5.2-Codex
sources.evidence: December 18, 2025 original card, retrieved as a complete PDF. Describes this exact coding variant, compaction and RL training with simulated conflicting user edits in section 4.2.2. Does not disclose total or active parameters or a complete production network architecture. Reopened original PDF, searched its full extracted text and read introduction/training sections on October 27; introduction explicitly identifies the GPT-5.2 version relationship. The specialization and RL sections supply no nominal size from which to infer counts.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Guide explicitly applies to models before GPT-5.6. Explains cached key/value projections in Transformer attention layers and includes an exact gpt-5.2-codex Responses compaction example. With exact-model prompt-caching support, supports only a broad Transformer inference, not a full block inventory or dense/MoE classification.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses PDF processing extracts text and page images for vision-capable models. Combined with this exact model reference’s vision and Responses support, establishes PDF as a supported API input format.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 deprecation section explicitly lists gpt-5.2-codex with a July 23, 2026 shutdown date.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.3-Codex
sources.evidence: February 5, 2026 announcement includes an exact GPT-5.2-Codex (xhigh) appendix comparison column. Its entries are benchmark scores, not total or active parameter counts. Reopened October 27; appendix distinguishes GPT-5.2-Codex (xhigh) from GPT-5.2 (xhigh), with only task success percentages.

sources.title: GPT-5.3-Codex System Card
sources.evidence: Later card retrieved as a complete PDF; includes exact GPT-5.2-Codex safety and capability comparisons, including CTF and CVEBench. These disclose evaluation results, not GPT-5.2-Codex parameter counts or a complete network architecture. Later sibling training claims are not transferred. Reopened original PDF and searched its full text on October 27; exact GPT-5.2-Codex comparison entries remain evaluation results rather than numerical model sizes.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current service terms grant limited service-use rights and reserve OpenAI intellectual property; used only to support a descriptive proprietary classification, not to reconstruct the terms in force at launch.

sources.title: OpenAI model catalog
sources.evidence: Lists GPT-5.2-Codex among hosted/retired models and separately identifies the gpt-oss open-weight models; no weight distribution or open-weight license is supplied for GPT-5.2-Codex.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27 to follow the explicitly named GPT-5.2 base lineage. December 11 launch distinguishes Thinking, Instant and Pro and maps Thinking to the gpt-5.2 API model. Describes capabilities, training and benchmark results but publishes no total or active parameter count to inherit for GPT-5.2-Codex.

sources.title: GPT-5.2 System Card
sources.evidence: Original 27-page PDF reopened October 27; full extracted text searched and Model Data and Training section read. Discusses datasets, reinforcement learning and safety evaluations for GPT-5.2, without disclosing a nominal total or active size. The accepted named base relationship therefore supplies no numerical count for the Codex variant.

sources.title: Step 3.5 Flash: Open Frontier-Level Intelligence with 11B Active Parameters
sources.evidence: Freshly opened original February 2026 technical report, section 6.2 comparison table: separate Activated params and Total params rows both give a dash for GPT-5.2 xHigh. This is the StepFun team's comparison, not an OpenAI disclosure; the label is the general GPT-5.2 model rather than GPT-5.2-Codex, so it supplies no exact Codex count or base count to inherit.

name.note: Use the exact official hyphenated product name.

developer.note: OpenAI published the model announcement and original system card.

family.note: The exact model is expressly a GPT-5.2 version optimized for coding; family classification follows the base generation.

release_date.note: Earliest public Codex release was December 18, 2025, not the December 11 release of general GPT-5.2. Responses API availability followed January 14, 2026.

open_weights.note: Released through hosted Codex and subsequently the API. The reviewed first-party release, model reference and catalog provide no downloadable weights and distinguish gpt-oss as open-weight.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted OpenAI model; no named open-weight license is disclosed. Current service terms support this classification but do not establish historical launch contract wording.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 parameter-only review reopened the exact launch/reference, original Codex card, named GPT-5.2 base launch/card and later GPT-5.3-Codex comparisons. The explicit GPT-5.2 version relationship is valid lineage evidence; reviewed specialization, vision and compaction descriptions state no pruning, distillation or expert expansion, but neither the variant nor its named base has a published nominal total to inherit. StepFun's later separate total/activated comparison lists GPT-5.2 xHigh as a dash, not a count. Targeted fresh exact-model and base searches found no usable later primary disclosure. Null reflects missing numerical evidence, not a demand for an exact tensor census or deployment attestation.

active_parameters_b.note: Active count was rechecked independently on October 27. Neither original exact-model sources nor later OpenAI exact-model comparisons publish an activated-parameter figure. The original StepFun comparison explicitly separates activated from total parameters but leaves both GPT-5.2 xHigh entries blank; it is not a Codex count and provides no numerical base convention to inherit. Bounded fresh searches found no original model-team table or plot assigning an active count to this exact variant. No total-equals-active assumption is made.

architecture.note: Qualified operational inference: the exact model reference explicitly supports prompt caching; the applicable pre-GPT-5.6 Prompt Caching 201 guide explains Transformer attention key/value reuse and includes an exact gpt-5.2-codex example. This supports a broad Transformer classification only. Original/later cards and first-party training/interpretability leads did not disclose the complete production block inventory, dense versus MoE structure, layer/head counts or numerical size.

context_window.note: Last-documented context window is 400,000 tokens; exact reference also specifies 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output. Compaction permits cumulative work across requests and does not enlarge the per-request context. Documentation is historical capability evidence, not proof of an operating endpoint.

modalities.note: Native documented model modalities are text/image input and text output. PDF is retained as an API input format: the file-input guide processes PDF text and page images for vision models via Responses, both explicitly supported by this exact model. No native audio/video input or image/audio output is asserted.

reasoning.note: Exact reference lists reasoning token support and low, medium, high and xhigh effort settings; no none setting is borrowed from general GPT-5.2.

tool_call.note: The exact model reference explicitly lists function_calling as a feature and supported Responses tool.

description.value: GPT-5.2 coding variant with reasoning, text and image input, function calling and context compaction.
description.note: Plain description restricted to exact-model documented capabilities; avoids unsupported ranking and network-size claims.

patch.name: GPT-5.2-Codex
patch.description: GPT-5.2 coding variant with reasoning, text and image input, function calling and context compaction.

sources.label: Addendum to GPT-5.2 System Card: GPT-5.2-Codex
Step 3.5 Flash: Open Frontier-Level Intelligence with 11B Active Parameters

patch.notes: Released in Codex on 2025-12-18; Responses API release was 2026-01-14. The undated gpt-5.2-codex identifier is not an immutable dated checkpoint; the reviewed reference gives no separately dated target or complete alias history. Last-documented limits are 400,000 context, 272,000 maximum input and 128,000 maximum output tokens. Compaction does not enlarge that context window. PDF is an API input format processed into text and page images. Transformer is a qualified inference from exact-model prompt-caching support and the applicable first-party caching mechanism; dense/MoE structure and full block inventory remain undisclosed. Total and active parameter counts remain undisclosed: OpenAI explicitly identifies this as a GPT-5.2 coding variant, but neither the variant nor its named base has a supported nominal count in the reviewed sources. The API was deprecated on 2026-04-22 and shut down on 2026-07-23; the current model reference says Shut down. No live endpoint request was made, and this API retirement date is not asserted as a separate Codex product retirement date.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains null total and active counts after reopening original sources, checking the explicit GPT-5.2 lineage and searching later disclosures and activated-parameter comparisons. The lineage is accepted, but no supported numerical base size is available to inherit; StepFun's later GPT-5.2 xHigh total/activated rows are both dashes, and later OpenAI exact Codex comparisons are benchmark scores. Added explicit parameter patches and source state; preserved the other 12 assessments and prior corrections to identity, release, capabilities and API retirement.
